# A. Structure-Mapping / Analogy Ontology

This is much richer than the ordinary expression

Forbus, Mostek and Ferguson explicitly construct an **analogy ontology** based on Gentner's structure-mapping theory so analogical operations can coexist with ordinary logical inference. Importantly, analogy can generate correspondences/conjectures while first-principles reasoning can subsequently validate them. ([AAAI Press](https://www.aaaipress.org/Library/AAAI/2002/aaai02-130.php?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Native representation

Abstractly:

$$
\mathcal C=(E,P,R)
$$

where a case contains entities $E$, properties/predicates $P$, and-most importantly-relations $R$.

Given

$$
\mathcal C_A,\mathcal C_B,
$$

the interesting object becomes a mapping

$$
M:\mathcal C_A\dashrightarrow\mathcal C_B
$$

that preserves a relational organization.

### Zoom out

$$

+\text{relations}
+\text{correspondences}
+\text{mapping}
+\text{candidate inference}
+\text{independent validation}
}
$$

This is **not** itself a physical law.

It is a formal language for asking:

> Which structural content survives translation between domains?

**witness correspondence.**

Very strong clip.

That produces a second-order object.

Relational comparison:

# C. Isomorphism

Now we can sharpen what we've loosely called cross-domain recurrence.

For structured systems

$$
\mathcal A=(A,\Omega_A),\qquad
\mathcal B=(B,\Omega_B),
$$

an isomorphism is a bijective map

$$
\phi:A\rightarrow B
$$

preserving the relevant structure.

For an operation:

$$
\boxed{
\phi(f_A(x,y))
=
f_B(\phi(x),\phi(y))
}
$$

or for dynamics:

$$

\phi\circ T_A=T_B\circ\phi.

This is substantially stronger than analogy.

$$

\text{carrier A}
+\text{structure A}
+\phi
+\text{carrier B}

+\text{preservation law}
}

Hence we should stop asking only:

and ask:

$$
\boxed{
\exists\phi:
\phi T_A=T_B\phi\;?
}

That is a **much stronger falsifiable question**.

And importantly:

$$
\text{analogy}\not\Rightarrow\text{isomorphism}.
$$

So this block simultaneously gives SUN a language **and a brake**.

# D. Isomorphic Systems Processes / Systems Processes Theory

This is different from mathematical isomorphism.

The ISP/SPT literature is trying to identify **processes recurring across systems and disciplines**. The source in your collection describes at least 55 candidate process classes condensed from 110 individual processes, with a larger descriptive schema for characterizing them. ([MDPI](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/6/2/18?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

The particularly useful move is:

$$
\text{objects}\longrightarrow\text{processes}.
$$

Instead of classifying a system by what it contains, classify it by what it **does**.

### Representation

A process can be treated approximately as

$$
P=
(F_{\rm feature},
F_{\rm function},
P_{\rm processivity},
M_{\rm measurable},
\dots).
$$

The actual ISP work explicitly uses categories including **Features, Functions, Processivity and Measurables**. ([MDPI](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/6/2/18?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

\text{system}

\rightarrow

\text{cross-domain ISP}

Meaning SUN could distinguish:

from the larger dynamical role or process family instantiated by $T$.

That's another real socket.

# E. Monterey Phoenix - perhaps the cleanest formal LEGO

This one deserves special attention.

Monterey Phoenix defines behavior from **events** and uses two fundamental relations:

$$
\boxed{\text{precedence}}
$$

and

$$
\boxed{\text{inclusion}}.
$$

Precedence determines event ordering; inclusion provides event decomposition. From the behavioral grammar MP generates a **scope-complete set of possible event traces**-exhaustive up to a user-defined event-iteration bound. ([MDPI](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/6/2/18?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

So the primitive is not:

$$
x.
$$

It is effectively:

$$
e_i\prec e_j
$$

and

$$
e_j\subset e_i.
$$

### Zoom out

$$
\boxed{
\text{events}
+
\text{precedence}
+
\text{inclusion}
+
\text{composition}
\rightarrow
\text{event traces}
\rightarrow
\text{possible behaviors}
}
$$

This is remarkably close to SUN's move from static values toward trajectories.

Current SUN:

\xrightarrow{R}

\xrightarrow{L}
\frac12C_n=C_{n+1}.

$$

$$

versus

$$

versus parallel/alternative/composed paths.

And now something subtle becomes explicit.

We know:

$$
RL=LR=\frac12
$$

numerically.

But:

$$
\boxed{RL=LR}
$$

does **not necessarily mean that the two paths are behaviorally identical**.

SUN currently has excellent language for operator closure.

MP offers better language for **trace structure**.

That's a new block, not a synonym.

# F. System-Dynamics Archetypes

Here “archetype” has a rigorous systems meaning rather than the Jungian one.

Wolstenholme reduces a large family of system archetypes to four generic structures generated by arrangements of **reinforcing** and **balancing feedback loops**. He additionally distinguishes problem and solution archetypes and emphasizes the location of the system boundary. ([Wiley Online Library](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/sdr.259?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Let

$$
R_f=+\text{ feedback},
\qquad
B_f=-\text{ feedback}.
$$

Then recurrent system organization comes from topological arrangements of these feedback structures.

### Zoom out

$$
\boxed{
\text{variables}
\rightarrow
\text{causal links}
\rightarrow
\text{loops}
\rightarrow
\{R_f,B_f\}
\rightarrow
\text{loop topology}
\rightarrow
\text{behavioral archetype}
}
$$

Even better, later work demonstrates that these archetypes can be **algorithmically detected** rather than merely eyeballed. ([Wiley Online Library](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/sdr.1526?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### SUN clip

SUN presently recognizes repeated transformations.

This framework asks whether the important invariant may sometimes be a **feedback topology** rather than a scalar ratio:

$$
\boxed{
\text{same dynamical topology}
\neq
\text{same numerical trajectory}.
}
$$

That could become relevant once SUN moves from operator pairs into larger dynamical systems.

Strong block, but downstream of A-E.

# G. Archetypal Analysis - completely different meaning of archetype

This is why we must preserve whole systems rather than collecting terminology.

In archetypal analysis, an archetype is an **extreme point characterizing the convex hull of data**. A dataset can then be reconstructed from those archetypal values. Stone and Cutler specifically apply this to spatio-temporal dynamics. ([ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0167278995002448?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

If archetypes are

$$
z_1,\ldots,z_k,
$$

then observations can approximately be represented as convex mixtures:

$$
\boxed{
x_i\approx
\sum_{j=1}^{k}\alpha_{ij}z_j
}
$$

subject to

$$
\alpha_{ij}\ge0,
\qquad
\sum_j\alpha_{ij}=1.
$$

And the archetypes themselves lie on/extremely near the convex hull.

### Zoom out

$$
\boxed{
\text{observations}
\rightarrow
\text{state space}
\rightarrow
\text{convex hull}
\rightarrow
\text{extreme archetypes}
\rightarrow
\text{mixture coordinates}
\rightarrow
\text{reconstruction}
}
$$

This is not currently native to SUN.

But it offers a powerful future empirical question:

> Given many observed SUN witnesses, are the apparent manifestations mixtures of a smaller set of extremal relational regimes?

That is legitimately interesting-but unlike B/E, it doesn't clip directly onto the present core.

Put it on the table, **do not snap it in yet**.

# H. Functional Recategorization

Veale attacks another problem relevant to SUN: ordinary taxonomies categorize objects by conventional identity, while analogy may require categorizing them according to **behavior and functional potential**. ([ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/I05-1029/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Thus:

$$
x\in C_{\rm nominal}
$$

can be replaced by something more like

$$
x\in C_{\rm functional}(f).
$$

Two things that look categorically unrelated may therefore belong together under a functional abstraction.

### Zoom out

$$
\boxed{
\text{entity}
\rightarrow
\text{semantic properties}
\rightarrow
\text{functional potential}
\rightarrow
\text{recategorization}
\rightarrow
\text{cross-category analogy}
}
$$

SUN already says:

> units are carriers.

$$
\boxed{
\text{classify by relational function, not carrier identity}.
}
$$

So:

music interval,

W72 operation,

geometric transformation,

sequence transition

need not share a nominal category.

They may instantiate the same **functional relational category**.

That is exactly the kind of abstraction SUN needs, although Veale's particular NLP implementation is not itself something SUN should inherit wholesale.

**That is the pile of LEGOs I think you were asking for.**

and in log coordinates,

The W72 reciprocal witness supplies the inverse composition:

SUN therefore **doesn't primarily lack arithmetic**.

A semantic type system, preventing false equivalences.

A genealogy recorder, retaining multiple paths to apparently similar outputs.

A constraint engine, recording what must remain invariant and what cannot be validly composed.

A prediction engine, generating testable expectations and negative results.

# SUN / SOL: orientation atlas and development decision

**Research checkpoint: 18 October 2026.** This report advances the declared mathematical and textual models; it does not claim that the whole project has one uniquely established orientation.

## 1. Outcome

The project now has a reproducible distinction between source facts, mathematical impossibilities, permitted extensions, and choices that evidence has not selected. The strongest completed results are:

1. The Exodus extraction gives **70 distinct original-glyph triplets and 69 distinct normalized triplets**. The counts refer to different representations. Gate 39 contains a genuine ordered-letter discrepancy in the selected display dataset; the derived tables correct it to **רהע**.
2. Under an explicitly optional requirement that two translations generate all of W72, **5,184 ordered pairs reduce to 1,152**, forming **three equivalence classes** under the full group automorphism action. The declared 5/7 angular steps leave **12** transitive phase completions.
3. The recovered phase-preserving SUN projection remains coherent. Its six cycles of length twelve do not fail a requirement it never adopted. Transitive phase completions are an additional model family.
4. A historical **221/442 sequence-system gate rule** is a legitimate alternative to the **231/462 letter-pair gate rule**. A counting unit is now a required parameter.
5. Complete legion-count vectors give **2,648** for the selected repository, **2,645** for the 1916 de Laurence transcription, and **2,618** for Peterson's Sloane 3825 main transcription. A textual witness is now a required parameter.
6. All **792** upper seven-subsets have constructive extensions to a lower seven/five correspondence when the connecting bijection is free. None preserves all four upper triads intact. These are two distinct comparison contracts.
7. New clock and cover constructions preserve the declared SUN relations. The checks cover **83,592 clock states** and **432 cover addresses**. An obstruction in W72 need not be an obstruction in an extended model.

The code and every enumerated candidate are supplied. This moves the project from repeated numerical suggestions to a finite, inspectable decision space in the parts whose rules are defined.

## 2. Authority and scope

Your current instruction permits new operations and parameters if established systemic relationships survive. The recovered direct user correction also assigns different jobs to the projects: **SUN supplies the rigid mathematical relations; SOL studies relations across scales and traditions, including structures outside a fixed torus.** The selected Bible-Astrology repository is an authorized base orientation for the current display. That authorization does not independently validate all its historical correspondences.

The audit used the ten supplied files, key decisions and relevant passages in the three supplied long histories, the recovered *SUN and SOL Frameworks* history, the revised SUN constitution, and the primordial crosswalk. These histories contain substantial cross-project material, but this is not a claim to have read the complete account histories of AYLI, ARIADNE, THREAD, CHORD, KEYSTONE, ARGO, BEANS, ROSETTAS TONES, or DOVES. The separate authority and coverage register records what was recovered. Earlier model-produced declarations of “locked” were checked against direct user corrections and later evidence.

A missing source is marked **NOT RETRIEVED**, rather than treated as false. A source claim incompatible with a specified reading is marked **CONTRADICTED IN THAT WITNESS**. A mathematical impossibility always names its assumptions. **UNSUPPORTED** does not mean **IMPOSSIBLE**.

The original music-native derivation predicting a 70-object quotient was not recovered. The textual 70 count is now independently reproduced; this does not establish the missing musical derivation. The original phase-contract attachment cited by a recovered assistant passage was also not retrieved. The phase-preserving profile is therefore a recovered transcript profile, with its source dependency visible.

The selected Sefirot method was applied as a host-adapted review of goals, dependencies, reproducibility, claims, consistency, alternatives, falsifiers, simpler extensions, types, and synthesis. Mathbox supplied the bounded computation and evidence record; Precise Special Functions independently checked Γ(73)=72!. No callable AgentJev Decisions capability surfaced in the available tools, so the decision reconciliation is explicit in this report and its register.

## 3. What an orientation must specify

An orientation is a model record, not just a rotation. Use

\[
\theta=(M,w,u,X,A,G,\phi,h,\chi,\eta),
\]

where M selects the model family, w the textual witness, u the counting unit, X the state space, A the permitted actions, G the relabelings treated as equivalent, φ the source-to-state map, h the observation/normalization rule, χ any line-label monodromy, and η additional parameters such as clock, register, seam or tuning residual.

Each candidate also states which relations its map preserves: order, adjacency, group operation, parentage, association, jurisdiction, polarity, or another explicitly defined relation. Equality of counts supplies none of those relations by itself.

The total space is an open collection of typed model families. Within the finite families below the enumeration is exhaustive. The space of all as-yet-unspecified operations, witnesses and cross-tradition maps is not a finite list, so neither an exhaustive elimination claim nor a normalized probability over that whole space is presently justified.

### Useful exact families

| Declared family | Exact size | What is fixed |
|---|---:|---|
| Bijections of 72 indexed items to 72 addresses | 72! ≈ 6.1234×10^103 | Only distinctness and cardinality |
| Origin-preserving automorphisms of Z12×Z6 | 384 | Group structure |
| Affine group maps | 27,648 | Group structure, with translated origin |
| Permutations commuting with recovered R and L | 2,149,908,480 | Each named action fixed |
| Also commuting with binary flip B | 82,944 | R, L and B fixed |
| Also commuting with ternary shift T, instead of B | 2,592 | R, L and T fixed |
| Commuting with R, L, B and T | 72 | All four named actions fixed |
| Also fixing the origin | 1 | The preceding structure and its reference point |

These are different, overlapping contracts, not independent factors to multiply. The centralizer counts use the free-action formula |H|^m m! for m equivalent H-orbits. A coordinate relabeling that moves every label with it is a gauge change; moving a map against fixed historical or display labels can change a claim.

## 4. The exact SUN classification

The retained scalar rules are

\[
R(C)=\tfrac23 C,\qquad L(C)=\tfrac34 C,\qquad O(C)=\tfrac12 C,
\qquad RL=LR=O.
\]

The address group is W72=Z12×Z6≅Z12×Z3×Z2. Scalar value, address, source identity and path history remain separate. All finite orders below are **address-action orders**, not orders of the complete scalar operations.

### 4.1 Optional transitive translation model

Let R=(a,b), L=(c,d), and O=R+L. Requiring ⟨R,L⟩=W72 is equivalent to

\[
\gcd(ad-bc,6)=1.
\]

This follows by testing spanning in W72/2W72 and W72/3W72. Independent enumeration verifies all 5,184 pairs:

| Verdict | Count |
|---|---:|
| Generates W72 | 1,152 |
| Fails the mod-2 test only | 1,920 |
| Fails the mod-3 test only | 792 |
| Fails both | 1,320 |

The 1,152 passing pairs form three free automorphism orbits, each of size 384:

| Class | ord(R) | ord(L) | ord(O) | Pair count |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| R has order six | 6 | 12 | 12 | 384 |
| L has order six | 12 | 6 | 12 | 384 |
| O has order six | 12 | 12 | 6 | 384 |

The Sylow components explain the result: Z4×Z2 has 24 ordered generating pairs and eight automorphisms, producing three classes; Z3×Z3 has 48 bases and 48 automorphisms, producing one. Their product gives the classification.

There are 48 feasible O addresses, each supporting 24 pairs. The exact test is gcd(O_p,O_q,6)=1. Merely checking the order of O is insufficient: eight addresses of order six still fail.

### 4.2 Retain the declared angular steps

Write R=(5,b), L=(7,d). The 36 phase choices generate W72 exactly when b+d≡1 or 5 modulo six. The complete twelve are:

Preserving p and binary polarity β=q mod 2 gives two classes of six: R preserves β while L flips it, or the reverse. Preserving p and τ=q mod 3 gives six classes. Fixing p, τ and β leaves twelve distinct candidates. The allowed p-preserving maps are (p,q)↦(p,cp+dq), with c modulo six and d=±1; preserving β additionally requires even c.

The recovered phase-preserving profile instead has R=(5,0), L=(7,0), O=(0,0). It yields six twelve-cycles. It remains lawful in that profile. Selecting one of the twelve transitive completions requires a purpose for phase transport and independent evidence about its labels.

### 4.3 Fixed twelve-position wheel

For g(p)=εp+r, ε=±1, there are 24 dihedral candidates. Fixing polarity P(p)=p mod 2 leaves twelve. Fixing element E(p)=p mod 4 leaves three rotations, r=0,4,8. Element preservation already implies polarity preservation, so those filters are not two independent confirmations. Adding the imported Aries reference p=0 leaves one display orientation. This proves uniqueness under those fixed labels, not historical uniqueness of the labels themselves.

### 4.4 Orientation characters

For the cover (n,q)↦(n mod 12,q), the deck group is Z. Its two characters into {+1,−1} are χ(k)=1 and χ(k)=(−1)^k. Both are permitted by the currently declared character model. A twisted real line-label bundle does not make the ordinary torus nonorientable. The forward/reverse/forward textual extraction does not select a character without an independently specified row-to-sheet bridge.

## 5. Textual reconstruction: the repaired 72/216 dataset

The selected source is [Exodus 14:19–21 at Mechon-Mamre](https://mechon-mamre.org/p/pt/pt0214.htm), checked against the verse data in the [selected repository](https://github.com/khrollo963/Bible-Astrology). The extension criterion is a commuting projection. If π:X'→X forgets additional state, every retained old operation A must have a lift A' satisfying

Its scalar multiplier and required old relations must also survive. Additional operations may introduce further relations; their scope must be explicit. This criterion demonstrates compatibility with the declared contract, not with unknown future requirements.

### Clock extension

Use X'=X×Z_N, with old operations leaving the clock alone. A new tick is

\[
Q_a(C,p,q,t)=(C,p+a_p,q+a_q,t+1\bmod N).
\]

It closes after N ticks exactly when Na=0 in W72. We verified every address/clock state for N=72,360,364,365, with exact scalar descriptors and all named commutation and projection relations.
